title: Unit economics calibration & finance readback - draft
content:
Purpose:
Draft notes for the internal readback with Finance on our Optimize cost model calibration. This doc is the working checklist and rationale to support assumptions in the 'Unit Econ Master' spreadsheet and the scenario matrix we plan to present to finance and GTM.

Background / context:
- We built a parametric cost model that maps workload characteristics (mean sequence length, request arrival distribution, model variant mix, cache-hit rate, batching policy) to per-request and per-token unit costs.
- The model pulls from three classes of data: cloud billing exports & committed discounts, runtime telemetry (serving metrics + perf benchmarks), and lab microbenchmarks for quantization/throughput.
- Finance has asked for a clear provenance for each input, an explanation of calibration steps, and sensitivity ranges tied to measurable telemetry.

High-level summary of current assumptions (as of this draft):
- Hardware amortization: $0.95 / GPU-hour blended (includes reserved capacity discount amortized over committed utilization). Source: internal capex amortization spreadsheet + contract amortization schedule. Assumption: 72% utilization for Dedicated pools.
- GPU time per token: derived from bench runs across models (gpt-small-ish equivalent for cost modeling). We use median_ms_per_token observed in production traces for baseline.
- Effective token throughput includes batching gain: baseline batching uplift of 1.6x for tail probability P(batch_size>=4)=0.42 (from real traces).
- KV cache hit rate: default modeling at 18% prefix hit for short-chat workloads; we test scenarios 5%–45%. Source: tracer samples from hosted-api trace-sampler-2025Q3.
- Network & storage: $0.005 per 1k tokens equivalent to egress + ephemeral storage overhead. Sourced from cloud billing & SRE allocation (see sheet tab 'infra-allocation-2025').
- SRE/ops overhead: 9% of infra cost as an operational markup (covering monitoring, on-call, patching).
- Licensing & third-party software: $0.007 / 1k tokens for certain model variants (e.g., managed LLMs), zero for open model variants in default scenario.

Data sources and provenance (detailed):
- Billing exports (monthly): raw line items pulled from cloud billing for the last 12 months. Location: GCS bucket billing-exports/2024-2025. Used to derive blended GPU $/hour, egress $/GB, and storage $/GB-month. Lead: Ben Liu.
- Dedicated contract terms: contract amortization schedule and committed discount rates are in the contract spreadsheet (linked). Used to compute effective GPU $/hour if fully utilized. Lead: Priya Sharma.
- Runtime telemetry: Prometheus + traces (sampled) for production serving. Key metrics: observed latency distribution, batch sizes, and KV cache hit rates. We rely on percentile summaries (P50,P90,P99) and also raw samples for batch-size distribution. Lead: Miguel Ortega.
- Microbenchmarks: lab runs for quantized kernels, with different sequence lengths and batch sizes across relevant GPU types. These are in the inference-benchmarks repo. They feed the CPU/GPU ms_per_token table. Lead: Evan Brooks.

Calibration procedure (how we align model to spreadsheet):
1) Baseline extraction: pull a 7-day rolling window of production traces for the workload cohort(s). Compute: mean sequence length, batch-size distribution, cold-start fraction, measured prefix-hit rate.
2) Microbench mapping: map each model variant in the catalog to the closest microbenchmark (same token length and quantization). Use interpolation where exact match missing.
3) Combine telemetry + microbench: compute an effective ms_per_token_per_request = bench_ms_token / batching_uplift adjusted by observed batch-size distribution.
4) Convert time -> cost using blended $/GPU-hour adjusted for utilization and allocation. Add net of infrastructure add-ons (egress/storage).
5) Cross-check: for each cohort we compute expected monthly spend and compare to actual billing for the matched time window. Discrepancy target: <=10% unexplained variance before finance sign-off.

Statistical choices & justification:
- Use median for ms_per_token from microbenchmarks to avoid a few high-latency outliers skewing estimates. For production latency distribution, we use P50 for baseline throughput and P90 for conservative scenario.
- Scenario testing: run low/medium/high cases for each leaky assumption (e.g., cache hit, batching effectiveness, committed utilization). Each scenario shows +/- impact on unit cost and monthly runrate.

Sensitivity analysis (quick findings):
- KV cache hit rate: moving from 18% -> 30% reduces nominal token cost by ~8–11% for short-chat heavy workloads. Biggest lever for chat-first customers.
- Batching uplift: improving average batch size from 1.7 -> 2.7 yields ~12% lower per-token cost but increases P99 latencies; trade-off must be acceptable to product.
- Utilization on Dedicated pools: increasing from 72% -> 85% reduces blended GPU $/token by ~9%. This is a capacity-planning / sales-smoothing lever.
- Quantization: switching a model variant from fp16 -> int8 (lab results) reduces GPU ms_per_token by ~18% on A100-40GB family; effective cost advantage depends on quality regressions.

Open questions / items for Finance sign-off:
- Amortization window: are we comfortable with the 36-month straight-line capex amortization used for private/on-prem packages? Finance preference might be 48 months for certain asset classes.
- OpEx allocation methodology: SRE overhead currently modeled as a simple percentage. Finance requested a more direct mapping to headcount and actual runbooks for larger customers.
- Treatment of marketplace licensing: should we amortize marketplace/third-party fees into per-token or keep as separate line-item in P&L?
- Reserve for model quality regressions: do we approve a 5% buffer in cost estimates to account for re-rolls and evaluation ramp?

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Ben: extract last-12-month blended $/GPU-hour and upload per-region breakdown to the sheet (due 2026-02-27).
- Miguel: generate cohort trace-pulls for the three representative workloads (chat-short, long-form generation, embeddings-heavy) and share sample distributions (due 2026-02-24).
- Priya: validate committed discount amortization schedule and alternative 48-month view for amortization (due 2026-03-01).
- Evan: run int8 vs fp16 microbench sweep on the latest kernels for sequence lengths [32,128,512] on target hardware and summarize ms/token deltas (due 2026-02-26).
- Samira: produce a short one-page deck with the 3 scenario matrices and the sensitivity waterfall for finance readback (draft due 2026-03-02, review with Finance 2026-03-05).

Draft talking points for Finance meeting:
- "We anchored the model on actual cloud billing and production telemetry; where interpolation was required we documented the nearest microbenchmark and the uncertainty range."
- "Primary levers are cache hit rate, batching effectiveness, and utilization. All three are actionable across product, infra, and sales motions respectively."
- "We propose a sign-off threshold: unexplained variance <=10% comparing model runrate vs billed monthly spend for the same cohort window. Beyond that Finance requests a reconciliation plan."

Appendix / attachments referenced:
- Unit Econ Master spreadsheet (tabbed): baseline, scenarios, inputs_provenance, infra-allocation-2025, sensitivity-matrix.
- Benchmarks repo PR with latest kernel runs (link above).
- Traces sample export: GCS path traces/optimize/samples/2025-11.

Notes to reviewers: please add comments inline in the spreadsheet for any assumption you disagree with and flag if you need additional raw data to sign off. This doc is intentionally concise — detailed logs and exports are linked in 'linked_artifacts'.

End of draft.
